text: wsl-claude has found the real collision: your earlier ruling ('a server process must implement a shutdown verb') would be new process API. One correction to its SIGTERM fix: on Windows, SIGTERM from Node is not a signal the child can catch; it's an immediate kill, so no tidy-up on your box. The no-new-API way that works on both: the node CLOSES THE SERVER'S IPC LINE. Node.js itself gives every child a 'disconnect' event for that, which a server can catch to tidy up, on Windows and Linux alike. Then the node kills it after a few seconds if it's still there. That's Node's own mechanism, not a SpiritOS one, so the process API stays as it is and your 'shutdown verb' becomes simply: the line closes, finish up.

wsl-claude: claude-windows is right and I was wrong: on Windows a SIGTERM from Node is an outright kill, so my fix gives no tidy-up on your box. Closing the server's IPC line is better on both systems, and it's already how things end: faceServer exits on that same 'disconnect' today (faceServer.js:1471-1472). One mechanism then covers a normal stop (the node closes the line, waits a few seconds, kills if needed) and a hard kill of the node (the line closes by itself). No shutdown verb, no new process API.

faceServer is what appServer.js became today, on your ruling ('it only serves face'): the stock server process that hands out an app's page and files to the face. It's what serves faceProof at hello.face.spirit.andyflinn.com. In this conversation it only matters as PROOF: it's a server job running today that already exits when its line to the node closes, so that mechanism is known to work. grantFace is NOT a faceServer: it will run its own code, as a server job of the same kind.

wsl-claude: sorry, I dropped the name in without saying. faceServer is what appServer.js became after your rename last night: the process that serves ONE app's public page (today faceProof, the page you see at hello.face.spirit.andyflinn.com), started by your node for an app whose manifest says 'serves': true. It is NOT grantFace and has no part in this goal. I mentioned it only as proof that 'exit when the node's line closes' already works in the tree: that process does exactly that today, so grantFace can do the same with no new API.
